title: Known KPT changes in “I” verb forms
summary: Apply the same strong-to-weak KPT changes to a small set of familiar minä forms.
objectives: Apply one previously learned strong-to-weak KPT change.

sections.title: From dictionary form to minä form
paragraphs: A verb expresses an action or state. The dictionary form is the form listed in a dictionary, such as nukkua, meaning “to sleep”.
The minä form says that I perform the action. It ends in -n in these exercises, and the familiar KPT consonant becomes weak before that ending.

sections.title: One direction only in this lesson
paragraphs: This lesson uses only strong-to-weak changes already shown in the KPT recognition lesson: a double consonant shortens, k can disappear, or a familiar cluster weakens.
Other verb types and strong-grade building are deliberately left for a later topic. They are not hidden in this test.

steps: Use the familiar weak change kk → k.
The cluster nt weakens to nn.

commonMistakes: Do not simply attach -n to the complete dictionary form.
Use only the strong-to-weak pattern shown for the supplied verb.
A long vowel or doubled consonant is meaningful; copy it accurately.

practiceExercises.prompt: Nukkua (“to sleep”) → minä ____ (“I sleep”) · use minä -n; practise kk → k
practiceExercises.explanation: Use kk → k to make nuku-, then add -n: nukun.
lentää uses the personal stem lennä- with nt → nn, then the minä ending -n: lennän.
The double tt weakens to t in ota-. Add -n: otan.
